gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: We inspected the four bridges, but ___ of them was safe.
gaps.explanation: 'None of them was ...' is used for three or more items; 'neither' is only for two.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
___ students joined the trip this year than last.
The village is remote and has ___ facilities — not even a post office.
gaps.hint: negative meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Few facilities' means almost none, which matches 'not even a post office'; 'facilities' is countable.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.

gaps.sentence: I'd love ___ help with the decorating, if you're free.
gaps.explanation: 'Some' is used in requests and hopes where the speaker wants agreement.
